feedback: Full answer: dinosaurs were real animals, not made up like dragons — we know because we find their fossils (real bones, teeth and footprints turned to rock); no people lived at the same time as non-bird dinosaurs; they died out a very, very long time before any people, and extinct means none are left alive anywhere.
If a child says dinosaurs are pretend: show fossils are real evidence you can see in a museum; we have never found dragon fossils.
If a child says cave people lived with dinosaurs: stretch the timeline so people are a dot at the very end, far after dinosaurs died out.

If a child says dinosaurs like T. rex are still alive/hiding: clarify 'extinct' means none left alive anywhere; distinguish from rare-but-living animals. If a child means birds, agree that birds are the one dinosaur group still alive today.
Offer a palaeontologist or museum-guide character to answer 'were they real?' and 'are any alive?' in child-friendly language if a conversational format helps engagement.
activities.intendedInsight: A full understanding holds all three: dinosaurs were real (evidence = fossils); non-bird dinosaurs like T. rex are extinct (none left alive anywhere); and they lived long before any people.
learnerActions: Respond to a friend's claim: 'Dinosaurs are just pretend, like dragons and unicorns — and anyway, cave people used to keep them as pets.' Is your friend right or wrong?
Explain how we can be so sure dinosaurs were real.
Say whether people ever lived at the same time as dinosaurs.

Answer the deeper questions: How do we know dinosaurs were real if nobody ever saw one alive? Was 'a long time ago' like when grandparents were little, or much, much longer? What does 'extinct' mean, and can you name another extinct animal?
